metadata.note: The Virginia Air Line Railway (chartered 10 Apr 1906, opened Oct 1908) was a 30-mile cut-off from the C&O main line at Lindsay to the James River Line at Strathmore, built for high/wide loads that could not clear the Blue Ridge tunnels. The C&O operated it from 1/2 July 1909 and bought it 12 July 1912, running it as the Virginia Air Line Branch / Sub-Division of the Richmond Division. One feature, in Chesapeake and Ohio colour, because every drawn year was C&O-operated; the Virginia Air Line ran its own trains only Oct 1908 - June 1909, when no passenger service is confirmed.
metadata.source: research/branches/virginia_air_line_railway.txt (2026-10-27): Daily, piedmontsub.com/VAL.shtml; ICC Inv. 2609 (1942); Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 15; Wikipedia; virginiaplaces.org; branchline.uk Virginia Railroads section 23; Alexandria Gazette 9 and 22 Sept 1909.
metadata.freight_only_check: Freight only from 24 June 1954 to the last train on 1 Aug 1973 (abandoned 3 Nov 1975); not drawn. The branch is not freight-only for its life despite Wikipedia's lead - mixed trains carried passengers to 1954.
metadata.ownership_split: Rule 4 split date is the C&O operating takeover, 1/2 July 1909 (the 1912 sale did not change who ran the trains). All drawn years (1927-1954) are C&O, so no split feature. If 1908-09 passenger service is ever sourced, add a separate Virginia Air Line Railway feature on the same geometry for Oct 1908 - June 1909.
not_yet_sourced: Passenger service 1908-1926: the line opened Oct 1908 and depots (Fork Union, Palmyra 1909) suggest passengers, but no source names a passenger train before Daily's 21 Feb 1927 entry. The start is drawn at 1927 (first confirmed year). Wanted: a 1909-1926 Official Guide C&O table, a C&O public timetable, or a Fluvanna newspaper item.

1951 extent: Official Guide Table 15 (schedule 31 March 1951) shows mileages 0/9/16 only in the OCR; whether the mixed then ran the full branch to Strathmore or was cut back (e.g. to Palmyra, 16.7 mi) is not established. Drawn as the full branch.
1954 end: the 23 June 1954 end of mixed service rests on Daily alone (Wikipedia copies it); not primary-confirmed. Without it the confirmed span would be 1927-1951 [OPEN].

Source conflict, purchase date: Alexandria Gazette 22 Sept 1909 says the C&O board would acquire the VAL on 19 Oct 1909; Daily and Wikipedia give 12 July 1912. Does not affect drawing (operation passed July 1909 either way).
C&O takeover day: Daily gives 1 July 1909 in prose and 2 July 1909 in his timeline.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), old_railway_operator=C&O lifted-grade ways, routed with opstrace.py, 2026-10-27
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap end to end, no straight-line legs: 29.2 mi drawn against 30.0 mi documented (branchline.uk Virginia section 23, Lindsay 0.0 - Strathmore 30.0) and 29.3 mi in ICC Inv. 2609 (1942). The whole branch survives in OSM as one chain of lifted-grade ways tagged old_railway_operator=C&O, name 'Chesapeake and Ohio': railway=razed way 334800906 Lindsay - Palmyra (27.6 km), then railway=abandoned ways 1341433474/1341433475, 633165641 and 1370764983-1370764986 Palmyra - Strathmore. Routed with opstrace (all 28.7 routed miles on C&O-tagged ways, max 36 m from the grade after simplification); the router's snap stopped 0.5 km short at Lindsay and 0.4 km short at Strathmore, so the last grade vertices were appended from the same OSM ways. Lindsay end is the grade's own end node, 31 m from the live C&O main line (OSM 'North Mountain Subdivision', the old Piedmont Sub); Strathmore end is a node of the live Rivanna Subdivision (James River Line, now Buckingham Branch), 41 m beyond the grade's end. Strathmore is not in Nominatim and was pinned at that junction; it lies about 2.6 mi west of Bremo Bluff village by straight line, against the report's 1.6 mi from Bremo station - the grade junction, not the geocode, sets the point. The drawn line passes 3.0 km west of the Nominatim point for Fork Union village and 1.3 km west of Zion Crossroads village: the grade, not the village centre, is what is drawn. This is the line's only alignment (built 1906-08, no relocations known), so no later-era alignment is drawn.

segments.note: C&O passenger train over the Virginia Air Line Branch, Lindsay (C&O Piedmont main line) - Zion - Troy - Wildwood - Palmyra - Carysbrook - Fork Union - Strathmore (James River Line). Start drawn at 1927, the first CONFIRMED passenger year: Daily's timeline records that on 21 Feb 1927 passenger service was 'reduced to one daily train in each direction', so service existed before and after that date. The line opened in October 1908 and the C&O took over operation 1/2 July 1909, but no source found names a passenger train 1908-1926; the start is deliberately drawn late (confirmed only) - extend it only on evidence. Ends 1 June 1932, when the passenger train was replaced (not discontinued) by a mixed train (Daily). headway_min 1440 = one train each way daily, from Daily's 1927 description; it is not from a printed timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Daily's timeline dates the 21 Feb 1927 reduction to one train each way (the first confirmed passenger year) and the 1 June 1932 replacement by a mixed train. Single secondary source, uncited on its page.
Larry Z. Daily, "Virginia Air Line: Lindsay to Strathmore", C&O Piedmont Subdivision, https://piedmontsub.com/VAL.shtml

segments.note: Mixed train (passengers carried with freight - counts as passenger service under Rule 1) from 1 June 1932 to 23 June 1954, when 'mixed train service ended' (Daily; Wikipedia: 'By June 1954, all remaining mixed train service had come to an end'). Independently confirmed by two primary sources: ICC Inv. 2609 - on 31 July 1942 westbound third-class mixed No. 403 (engine 2335, with a baggage-coach) collided head-on near Rockaway with eastbound freight Third 402; four employees killed, one passenger injured. And the Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedule of 31 March 1951) still prints Table 15 'Virginia Air Line Branch' with times; its index lists Lindsay, Whitlock, Zion, Troy, Palmyra and Carysbrook. The 1951 table's surviving mileages run only 0/9/16, so whether the 1951 mixed still ran the whole 30 mi to Strathmore or was cut back is NOT resolved; drawn as the full branch (Carysbrook, 20.5 mi, is in the index, which argues against a Palmyra cut-back). The 1954 end rests on Daily alone (not primary-confirmed). Freight continued to the last round trip on 1 Aug 1973; abandoned 3 Nov 1975 - not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 1440 (one mixed each way daily) is an estimate; frequency not sourced from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Daily dates the 1932 start and the 23 June 1954 end of mixed service; ICC Inv. 2609 (1942) and the 1951 Official Guide Table 15 independently confirm passenger-carrying trains in those years. The 1954 end is single-source (Daily); the headway is an estimate.
